quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whatever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes the bike unstable and harder to balance.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during the day, you should:

options.text: Stay on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing to be more visible to other drivers, even during the day.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you during turns. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of these should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and increase following distance at night. Use headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out signals a left turn or lane change to the left. Hand signals can be used instead of or with mechanical turn signals.

questions.question: After you enter a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep your speed steady or accelerate slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or accelerate slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep your speed steady or accelerate slowly through the turn.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up out of the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up or the wobble will get worse. Grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.

questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: Which gives the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that will not break protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from wind best?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses usually do not.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits and is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to be more visible.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips—less than five miles long—just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is usually to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up and increase the distance between you.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make them follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Change power suddenly in a turn.
Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, use both brakes:
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together to stop as quickly as possible. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves can make you drowsy and affect your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass another vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This improves your view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what lessens its effects?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing down suddenly so other drivers notice and have time to react.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only one brake, front or rear, should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.
